translations.literal: He memorialized: 'The Huai and the Yellow have from antiquity not run together.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'The Huai and the Yellow Rivers were never meant to run as one.

sentences.zh: 邇者修歸仁堤，開胡家溝，出睢湖之水；

translations.literal: Recently the Guiren embankment was repaired and the Hujia Ditch opened to release the waters of Sui Lake;
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Guiren dike was repaired and the Hujia Ditch opened to drain Sui Lake;

sentences.zh: 閉六壩，加築高家堰，出洪澤湖之水。

translations.literal: the six sluices were closed and the Gaojia Embankment heightened to release the waters of Hongze Lake.
translations.idiomatic: the six sluices were closed and the Gaojia Embankment raised to drive Hongze Lake water out.

sentences.zh: 此借淮敵黃不易之理。

translations.literal: This borrows the principle that the Huai is hard to pit against the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: This uses the old idea of turning the Huai against the Yellow.

sentences.zh: 然淮水入運者多，則敵黃仍弱。

translations.literal: Yet when much Huai water enters the Grand Canal, the force against the Yellow is still weak.
translations.idiomatic: But when too much Huai water enters the canal, the Huai still cannot master the Yellow.

sentences.zh: 舊設天妃閘，自淮、黃交會處至清江浦，凡為五閘，重運到時，更迭啟閉，過即下板鎖斷，是以全淮注黃。

translations.literal: Formerly the Tianfei Sluices were set up; from where the Huai and Yellow meet to Qingjiangpu there were five sluices in all; when transport grain arrived they opened and closed in rotation, and once past the boards were lowered and locked, so all the Huai was poured into the Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: The old Tianfei sluices from the Huai–Yellow confluence to Qingjiangpu had five gates that opened only for grain transport and then shut, sending the Huai into the Yellow.

sentences.zh: 其引入運河者，不過暫資濟運。

translations.literal: What was led into the Grand Canal was only to assist transport temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: Only a portion was diverted into the canal to help transport.

sentences.zh: 自改建草壩，淮、黃盡趨運河，清江浦民居可危。

translations.literal: Since grass sluices were rebuilt, Huai and Yellow waters all rush into the Grand Canal and the homes of Qingjiangpu are in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Since reed sluices were built, both rivers pour into the canal and Qingjiangpu is endangered.

sentences.zh: 宜复天妃閘舊制，使淮易敵黃，有裨大工。」

translations.literal: The old Tianfei sluice system should be restored so the Huai may more easily contend with the Yellow, benefiting the great works.'
translations.idiomatic: The Tianfei system should be restored so the Huai can hold its own against the Yellow and the great works benefit.'

sentences.zh: 疏下河督張鵬翮議行。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to River Director Zhang Penghe for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to River Director Zhang Penghe for action.

sentences.zh: 尋疏劾山東蒲台知縣俞宏聲以赦前細故，拘系監生王觀成，迫令自殺；

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized impeaching Yu Hongsheng, magistrate of Putai in Shandong, who for a petty matter before an amnesty had imprisoned the student Wang Guancheng and forced him to suicide;
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Yu Hongsheng, magistrate of Putai in Shandong, who before an amnesty jailed the student Wang Guancheng over a trifle and drove him to suicide;

sentences.zh: 巡撫王國昌僅以杖責解役結案，玩視民命。

translations.literal: Governor Wang Guochang only punished with the bamboo and closed the case through a runner, treating the people's lives lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Guochang merely had a runner beaten and closed the case, showing contempt for life.

sentences.zh: 命侍郎吳涵偕詵往按，宏聲坐奪官，國昌等議處。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Vice Minister Wu Han to go with Shen to investigate; Hongsheng was stripped of office and Guochang and others were dealt with by law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Vice Minister Wu Han with Shen to investigate; Hongsheng lost his post and Guochang was punished.

sentences.zh: 授鴻臚寺卿，再遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was again promoted to left vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and then left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，授貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year he was appointed governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year he was appointed governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「貴州田地俱在層岡峻嶺間，土性寒涼，收成歉薄，人牛種蓺維艱。

translations.literal: He memorialized: 'Guizhou fields are all among layered ridges and steep peaks; the soil is cold and yields are thin; men and oxen find planting hard.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: 'Guizhou fields lie on steep slopes in cold soil with poor yields; farming is desperately hard.

sentences.zh: 前撫臣王蓺因合屬田地荒蕪十之四五，減輕舊則，招徠開墾成熟，六年後起科。

translations.literal: Former Governor Wang Yi, because four or five tenths of the province's fields were wasteland, reduced the old rates, encouraged cultivation until maturity, and taxation began after six years.
translations.idiomatic: Former Governor Wang Yi, finding forty or fifty percent of land abandoned, cut old tax rates and allowed six years before taxing reclaimed fields.

sentences.zh: 有續報者亦如之。」

translations.literal: Where later reports came in, the same rule applied.'
translations.idiomatic: Later reports were treated the same way.'

sentences.zh: 疏下部，如所請。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries; as requested.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries approved as he asked.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，調湖北。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 疏劾布政使王毓賢虧帑，命解任。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeaching Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Yuxian for treasury deficits and ordered him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Yuxian for treasury deficits and had him removed.

sentences.zh: 尋以盤驗已完，奏免其罪。

translations.literal: Soon, because the audit was complete, he memorialized to waive his punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the audit showed the debt cleared, he asked that Wang be spared further punishment.

sentences.zh: 五十年，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year he was promoted to minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth year he became minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year he was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，乞休，命致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year he begged to retire and was ordered to leave office with honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year he retired with honors.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，卒，賜祭葬，諡清恪。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year he died; sacrificial burial was bestowed and posthumous title Qingke.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixty-first year, was granted state burial, and received the posthumous title Qingke.

sentences.zh: 子世倌，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shiguan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiguan has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：當三籓亂時，雲、貴、閩、粵，其發難地也；

translations.literal: The commentator says: When the Three Feudatories rebelled, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, and Guangdong were where trouble began;
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: When the Three Feudatories rebelled, Yunnan, Guizhou, Fujian, and Guangdong were where the trouble began;

sentences.zh: 蹂躪所及，湖南北、江西、四川，受害最甚。

translations.literal: where their ravages extended, Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, and Sichuan suffered most.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan, Hubei, Jiangxi, and Sichuan suffered most where the armies passed.

sentences.zh: 伊闢、王繼文撫雲南，從師而南，參與軍畫，其事已別見；

translations.literal: Yi Pi and Wang Jiwen pacified Yunnan, followed the army south, and took part in military planning—their affairs are treated elsewhere;
translations.idiomatic: Yi Pi and Wang Jiwen pacified Yunnan and campaigned south—their stories are told elsewhere;

sentences.zh: 雍建於貴州，締虞於四川，弘祚於廣東，騭於江西，犖承騭，詵遙繼雍建，兵後撫綏甚勤。

translations.literal: Yongjian in Guizhou, Diyu in Sichuan, Hongzuo in Guangdong, Zhi in Jiangxi, Luo following Zhi, and Shen distantly continuing Yongjian—all toiled diligently to pacify and comfort after the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yongjian in Guizhou, Diyu in Sichuan, Hongzuo in Guangdong, Zhi in Jiangxi, Luo following Zhi, and Shen carrying on Yongjian's work—all labored hard to restore order after the war.

sentences.zh: 大亂方定，起衰救弊，出水火，登袵席，偉哉諸人之功歟！

translations.literal: Great disorder had just been settled; to raise what was failing, save the people from fire and water, and set them on the mat and cover—how great are these men's achievements!
translations.idiomatic: When great disorder had barely ended, they lifted the ruined realm from fire and water back to safety—what magnificent service these men rendered!
